proof:
Let $P_\varepsilon=(0,h+\varepsilon)$ and fill to $\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{P_\varepsilon\})$. If $P$ was in an edge interior then $P_\varepsilon$ is strictly beyond the supporting line (which separates the interior point $0$ from that ray continuation). The strict supporting-edge inequalities against every other vertex persist for the two new edges $RP_\varepsilon,P_\varepsilon S$ and for the unaltered edges, except that $P_\varepsilon$ is exactly on the two new edges. If $P$ was a vertex, move it to $P_\varepsilon$; strict inequalities for the finitely many original edges against nonincident vertices persist, and the old $P$ remains in the hull since it is on $[0,P_\varepsilon]$ and $0$ remains interior. In either case the added pieces, up to null edges, are the two triangles $RPP_\varepsilon$ and $SPP_\varepsilon$.

Their areas are $D_{12}=r_x\varepsilon/2$ and $D_2=-s_x\varepsilon/2$, in the two adjacent open sectors with cap signatures $\{1,2\}$ and $\{2\}$ respectively. The strict signs on $R,S$ and $y>0,x+y>0$ on $PP_\varepsilon$ prove these signatures by linearity. Thus the fill adds $D=D_{12}+D_2$ in area and changes caps by $(D_{12},D,0)$. Only the positive vertical ray endpoint moves: the new triangles do not touch $y=0$ or $x+y=0$, and the intersection with $x=0$ is the old chord with $PP_\varepsilon$ appended.

Choose a linear functional $\ell$ uniquely maximized at $R$ and strictly inside its normal cone, so that it still uniquely exposes $R$ after the small fill. A fixed sufficiently shallow cap $\ell\ge\ell(R)-t_0$ of $K$ has positive area and is entirely in $x>0,y>0$; the analogous cap of the filled hull stays in that open quadrant for small $\varepsilon$. Indeed otherwise compactness and convergence of the hull to $K$ would put a limiting point of the fixed closed cap outside the quadrant. The fixed-depth cap of the filled hull contains the old cap, so its area exceeds $D$ for small $\varepsilon$. Parallel cap areas vary continuously from zero at $t=0$ to that fixed positive area, by nullity of lines, and a cut of area exactly $D$ exists. It removes only cap signature $\{1,2\}$ and avoids all three source lines, giving the stated changes. The removing depth tends to zero because each positive-depth old cap has fixed positive area. The removed region therefore shrinks to $R$ by compactness and unique exposure. This, together with $K\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(K\cup\{P_\varepsilon\})\subseteq K+\varepsilon B_2$, gives Hausdorff convergence: the new cut boundary approaches $R$, and points near $R$ have distance to the retained polygon bounded by their distance to that boundary. Both modifications avoid a fixed small ball about $0$.

Since $1/\sigma_2,1/\sigma_3$ are fixed and $1/\sigma_1$ decreases, $\lambda_1$ strictly decreases and each other weight increases. Every order statistic is coordinatewise nondecreasing in the three cap areas, so the sorted positive combination and the separate upper bounds cannot increase at fixed total area. The same construction in a permuted canonical frame is valid because coarea is the derivative of area in the scalar cap threshold; an invertible linear frame change multiplies the three coareas by a common positive Jacobian, hence preserves their normalized inverse weights.

statement:
Use the three normals $v_1=(1,0)$, $v_2=(0,1)$, $v_3=(-1,-1)$ through the interior mark $0$. For a planar convex body $K$, let $q_i$ be the cap areas, $\sigma_i=\mathcal H^1(K\cap v_i^\perp)/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $\lambda_i=(1/\sigma_i)/\sum_j(1/\sigma_j)$. Let $K$ be a convex polygon and $P=(0,h)$, $h>0$, its positive vertical ray endpoint. Suppose $P$ lies in the relative interior of an edge with consecutive vertices $R,S$, or is a vertex flanked by $R,S$ in counterclockwise order. Require $R=(r_x,r_y)$ with $r_x,r_y>0$, and $S=(s_x,s_y)$ with $s_x<0<s_y$ and $s_x+s_y>0$. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an actual nearby polygon with the same area and changes
$$
\Delta(q_1,q_2,q_3)=(s_x\varepsilon/2,0,0),\qquad
\Delta(\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\sigma_3)=(\varepsilon,0,0).
$$
The new polygon contains $0$ in its interior and converges to $K$ in Hausdorff distance. Thus $\lambda_1$ strictly decreases, the other weights increase, and an initially minimal $\lambda_1$ remains minimal. Any initially satisfied cap upper bounds of the form $q_i\le c_i|K|$ and the constraint $q_{\min}+q_{\mathrm{mid}}+q_{\max}/4\le |K|$ remain satisfied. Consequently this adjacent-sector endpoint geometry cannot occur at a local minimum of the selected inverse weight within the feasible polygon class. The corresponding statements hold after cyclically permuting the caps or interchanging the two coordinate axes.
title: An adjacent-sector polygon fill and shave decreases a selected inverse chord weight
